Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates enlargement of the central pulmonary arteries, specifically a prominent right descending pulmonary artery (diameter >16 mm), which is a classic radiographic sign of pulmonary hypertension associated with chronic pulmonary embolism. The cardiac silhouette appears relatively normal in size, making severe pulmonary hypertension with significant right heart failure less likely than mild-to-moderate disease.
